Done and pushed as 0040fa2 (main -> origin/main).

Finding (from the reporter's own machine, not inference): the session is Wayland and every persisted layout record holds x:0 y:0. That is not a stale value but the platform's only answer — a Wayland compositor owns placement, xdg-shell has no position request, `gtk_window_move` (what tao calls from `set_outer_position`) is a no-op, and `gtk_window_get_position` always reports the origin. No application can restore its own position there; the earlier size fix (a7371de) is what made size correct.

Delivered: `session_places_windows()` (Linux: an explicit GDK_BACKEND wins, otherwise the presence of WAYLAND_DISPLAY decides; cached once) gates both directions. `measure` clears the stored x/y instead of recording the meaningless origin, and `restore_window_layout` never asks a session that cannot place windows to move one. X11 — including XWayland via GDK_BACKEND=x11 — keeps storing and restoring the position, and Windows is untouched.

Verification: `cargo test --bin aworkit-desktop desktop_layout` 4 passed (new: clearing the position when the session cannot report one; the x11/wayland/GDK_BACKEND decision including a comma-separated list); `cargo check --release --all-targets` clean; frontend 79 files / 593 tests green. Also recorded in project memory. Not verifiable here: a real repositioning on a Wayland desktop cannot be exercised in this environment, and on Wayland the expectation itself must change.

Reported: the window position is still not restored after reopening Aworkit on Linux.

Investigated on the reporting machine: the session is Wayland (`loginctl` reports Type=wayland, WAYLAND_DISPLAY is set) and every persisted layout record — dozens of versions — holds `x: 0, y: 0`. That is the platform's answer, not a stale value: a Wayland compositor owns window placement, `xdg-shell` has no position request, `gtk_window_move` (what tao calls from `set_outer_position`) does nothing, and `gtk_window_get_position` always reports the origin. No application can restore its position on Wayland; Firefox/Thunderbird behave the same way.

Delivered: a session that cannot place windows stores no position and is never asked to move one, so the record is honest and a later X11 session is not misled by a (0,0) read from Wayland. X11 keeps recording and restoring the position (which the existing post-map `set_position` handles), including XWayland via `GDK_BACKEND=x11`. Size restore is unaffected on every platform.

Acceptance evidence: `cargo test --bin aworkit-desktop desktop_layout` 4 passed (new tests for clearing the position and for the x11/wayland/GDK_BACKEND decision); `cargo check --release --all-targets` clean; frontend suite 79 files / 593 tests green; commits 0040fa2 (this) and a7371de (the earlier size fix).

data.title: Store no window position on Wayland and keep X11 position restore
